summary: classifyAPIError now recognises Canvas Builder's own refusals and passes them to the agent word for word. An APIError whose body carries one of the gateway's messages becomes refusedErr(msg, status): exit code 9, an Error() that is exactly the gateway's sentence, and the {"error","code":9,"status","refused_by":"Canvas Builder"} envelope on stdout in --agent mode. The unknown-outcome message is the one exception; the exit-8 branch added by safe-retries already takes it. Separately, the 400-auth, 401 and 403 branches now route their hints through authHint, which drops them in Canvas Builder. rootFlags gains sandboxActive, set in newClient when the loaded config carries a sandbox profile.
reason:
Two problems, both in the generated classifier. First, every gateway refusal was being read as an HTTP status and relabelled: a held approval (403) came out as "permission denied", a quarantined course (423) as a plain API error, and the gateway's own sentence was buried inside "GET /api/v1/... returned HTTP 403: {...}". An agent branching on the exit code learned nothing about who stopped it or why, and exit 4 in particular told it authentication was missing. Decision D8 added exit 9 for exactly this: Canvas Builder stopped this, and the message is already the explanation.

Second, the auth hints tell the reader to export CANVAS_API_TOKEN and run doctor. In Canvas Builder the agent cannot change the token — Canvas Builder issues and manages it — so the hint is wrong, and worse, it is an invitation to go looking for a token with more reach than the agent is meant to have. ADR 0001 in the Canvas Builder repo is explicit that the guardrails assume a resourceful agent, so the CLI must not point one at a wider credential. The hints stay in the plain CLI, where they are the right advice.
known_limitations:
A refusal that arrives with a 5xx status is still retried before it is classified. The only gateway message that comes as a 5xx is "couldn't record this change" (503), whose own text asks the caller to try again in a moment, so the retries are wanted there; but they cost the backoff curve (about 7 s over four attempts) before exit 9 is reported, and the gateway sees four journal attempts rather than one. Left as it is because the alternative is to decide, inside the retry loop, which refusals are worth repeating.

The refusal is matched on APIError.Body, which has been through the response sanitizer and the credential masker by then. Neither touches a gateway message — they are plain English with no credential-shaped text — but a future masking rule that rewrote one would turn a refusal back into an ordinary API error. The pre-sanitizer body is matched in internal/client (see safe-retries), which is where a stricter check belongs if this ever matters.

refusedErr does not write the envelope itself, because it has no access to the flags; classifyAPIError calls writeRefusalEnvelope beside it. Task 5's own refusals, raised in PersistentPreRunE before anything is sent, have to do the same.

sandboxActive is set in newClient, so it is only true once a command has built a client. Every classifyAPIError caller builds one first, so the auth branches see it; the help path does not, and Task 5 sets it earlier in ensureSandbox for that reason.
validated_outcome:
go build ./... and go vet ./... clean; go test ./... passing across all eight packages on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1; go test -race ./internal/cli/ passing. golangci-lint run --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 reports nothing in the new test files, and in helpers.go and root.go only the pre-existing generated-code findings (unchecked fmt.Fprintln returns, and the generator's import order, which gofmt flagged on these files before this patch too).

New coverage. internal/cli/refusal_test.go: TestRefusalSurfacedUnchanged is Review Focus 7, one row per gateway message except unknown outcome, each with its status, asserting exit 9, the envelope's error/code/status/refused_by, "Error: <message>" on stderr, and that neither stream contains CANVAS_API_TOKEN or export. TestCanvasErrorKeepsCanvasText checks a Canvas 404 in the same envelope shape still exits 3 with Canvas's own text. TestSandboxAuthErrorHasNoTokenHint runs a Canvas 401 in both modes: exit 4 either way, the hint gone in Canvas Builder and still there in the plain CLI.

internal/cli/runcli_test.go adds runCLI, which runs RootCmd() with os.Stdout and os.Stderr swapped for drained pipes and returns stdout, stderr and the exit code. internal/gatewaytest/fake.go gains WorkspaceOpts.OmitSandbox, which writes the same layout with no sandbox key so a test can compare the two modes.

CodeRabbit reviewed the patch and raised one finding, false: that config.Config has no Profile field, so cfg.Profile could not compile, and newClient should test a new TOML-backed Sandbox bool instead. Both fields are already in HEAD from Task 1, and cfg.Profile is the right test of the two: sandbox = true with settings Load can't validate is a config error there, never a run in Canvas Builder, and Profile is the validated form Load attaches after every override. The review ran with --uncommitted, which shows it only this patch's diff.
